<text>
Scottish National Party Manifesto 1997 — Summary (under 500 words)

Core vision
- “Yes We Can”: Scotland is wealthy, pays more to London than it receives, and can fund better services through independence.
- Independence is the means to deliver jobs, social justice, strong public services and a modern European democracy.

Path to independence
- A majority of SNP MPs would trigger negotiations with the UK and EU, lasting 6–12 months, followed by a single-question referendum on the settlement; then elections.
- EU membership would continue; open borders with England; pensions/investments protected by EU rules.
- Full citizenship and residence rights for all current residents.

Constitution and governance
- Written constitution and Bill of Rights, including social rights (health, housing, education, decent work).
- Unicameral Parliament elected by proportional representation; vote from age 16; public petitions; strong committees.
- Reform the monarchy’s role and funding; abolish unelected influence (no House of Lords role).
- Local government entrenched in the constitution; PR for councils.

Economy, tax and jobs
- Aim for full employment: 100,000 extra jobs; national apprenticeship scheme.
- Business tax cuts over four years: corporation tax 33p→30p; small companies 23p→18p; abolish Class IV NICs; reformed business rates.
- Growth agenda: export unit, R&D fund, tourism promotion, defence diversification.
- Fair personal taxation: introduce 15p starter rate; widen basic rate band; remove NI ceiling for higher earners; cut VAT on domestic fuel to 5%.
- Adopt EU Social Chapter; introduce a minimum wage (half median male earnings); charter for trade union rights.

Social justice and health
- Increase child benefit; restore benefits for 16–17s.
- Pensioner package: +£3/£5 per week, Cold Climate Allowance, remove standing charges for utilities, end means-testing for residential care.
- NHS: end internal market; reintegrate dentistry; +£35m p.a.; national/local health commissions; audit and prevention focus; ban tobacco advertising and raise tobacco duty.

Law, order and consumer protection
- “Zero tolerance” for community crime; bolster Procurator Fiscal service; develop alternatives to prison and rehabilitation; national vehicle register; total handgun ban; strengthen food safety via an independent Food & Consumer Health Agency.

Education, housing, local services and culture
- Hire 700 teachers; repair schools; classroom ICT and universal school internet.
- Free nursery education for all 3–4-year-olds; restore student grants; expand training; support Gaelic/Scots and community faith studies.
- Housing: transfer 75% of council housing debt to central government; build 20,000 affordable homes; renovate substandard stock; protect new/improved stock from discounted Right to Buy; abolish water quangos.
- Broadcasting: create a Scottish Broadcasting Corporation; support film via “Scottish Screen”; launch “Scot-Lot” lottery (no scratch cards).

Rural, sectoral and environment
- Abolish feudal tenure; Land Commission; transparent land register; local control of shore/seabed.
- Agriculture: BSE traceability, CAP reform, rural diversification fund; strengthen fisheries via Regional Councils, conservation, processing support.
- Forestry: double woodland in 25 years; new National Forest Enterprise Board.
- Environment: strengthen SEPA; national targets; end nuclear reprocessing at Dounreay; shift to decommissioning/renewables; phase out nuclear power; invest in renewables and conservation; ensure fair gas network access.

Transport and telecoms
- Integrate transport; bring Scottish Railtrack assets into public ownership; electrify key lines; integrate bus/rail.
- Remove Skye Bridge tolls (move to shadow tolls, then public ownership); support ferries; adjust/abolish Air Passenger Duty in H&I; improve air links.
- Expand telecoms competition and rural connectivity; back distance learning and internet adoption.

Europe, world and defence
- Full EU membership with voting rights, more MEPs, and rotating presidency.
- Targeted diplomatic network; join UN, Commonwealth, Council of Europe; British Isles association.
- Scottish Defence Forces (army, navy, air force); remove Trident; phased withdrawal from NATO due to nuclear stance; peacekeeping college; defence diversification.

Finances
- Four-year, fully costed budget; claim of large relative fiscal surplus versus UK; inherit ~£38bn debt, with £6.6bn repayment in first four years.
- Redirect spending from Trident to services; fund tax cuts, investment, and social programmes while reducing debt.
</text>
